The Stroop model as a rail network

Miller and Cohen (2001) compare the PFC to a railroad switchman: it doesn't carry the trains, it sets which track they take. In their Stroop example (after Cohen, Dunbar and McClelland, 1990), color and word inputs travel along two pathways to shared responses. The word pathway is stronger, so naming the ink color only wins when a PFC task unit biases the color pathway.
